selfCaughtDefect.what: First implementation used the input placeholder "teammate@firm.com". A pre-existing regression guard in settings-modal.test.tsx ('ships NO fixture roster in the component') asserts the shipped file's source never matches /@bastrop-arch\.com|@structural\.co|@firm\.com/ -- a guard against comp fixture emails leaking into shipped code. The placeholder string matched @firm.com and failed that test on the first full test-suite run.
selfCaughtDefect.howCaught: Running the full pnpm test suite before committing, not by re-reading the diff -- exactly the class of check ENFORCEMENT.md's 'verify a check by violating it' section describes: an existing check fired on a real, if trivial, mistake rather than the mistake being caught by inspection.
selfCaughtDefect.fix: Changed the placeholder to "name@company.com", which matches none of the guarded domains. Re-ran the full suite; the specific test and all others passed.
selfCaughtDefect.notAScopeChange: This was a one-line placeholder string fix inside the same file already being edited for this dispatch; no additional files touched, no test loosened to admit the mistake.

Considered exposing a richer TeamInviteOutcome carrying the server's returned invitation (id, createdAt) for an optimistic row instead of a full refetch. Rejected: the 201 body's shape was never independently confirmed (CP1), so rendering fields from it would be exactly the 'raw source key defaulted into a resolution' pattern ENFORCEMENT.md prohibits. A refetch from the already-trusted roster GET is slower by one round trip but never risks displaying an invented shape.
